decision.title: Content that streams into a constructor; XSLT sweep 3 (packet )

body.p: , after , , , . Accepts 's Proposed item "content that streams into a constructor", as one mechanism of the shared evaluator and IR, used by XSLT and XQuery alike.

item.p: Receiving and delivering tasks (glossary , ; src/evaluator_machine_internal.h, "Delivering"): a document or element constructor (and SHALLOW_COPY of an element or document) whose content expression is not a enclosed list opens its node, sets its part task's receive function and pushes the content as a delivering task (sxml_evaluator_task.delivers_content). When a delivering task finishes, the machine hands its value to the nearest receiving task below and the task below gets (). Delivering passes on only where a value reaches the receiver unchanged: LET bodies and conditional branches (they replace their task), a content LET's bound expression, each body of a MAP (not a path's MAP, whose body may select JNodes), the body of a function a delivering call enters (not through a coerced function item: its COERCE_RESULT task delivers), and the template calls of a delivering APPLY_TEMPLATES (which delivers its separators itself). A try/catch body never delivers, so no caught error leaves part of a content behind. The order and the rules of XSLT 4.0, 5.7.1 and XQuery 4.0, 4.12.1.3 are those of the content sequence: the receiver adds each value as before (arrays flattened, atomic items joined within one enclosed expression, nodes copied, documents unwrapped, XTDE0410 and XQTY0024 from the same state).

Building into the receiver: a constructor in a delivering task builds its node in the receiver's tree when that is what copying a tree of its own would give (sxml_construction_open): the same rules and construction flags and copy-namespaces preserve; no-inherit becomes the element start's ignores_parent_namespaces; a document's children become the content. Text, attribute, comment and processing-instruction constructors add their node directly (a namespace node keeps its own tree, whose builder checks XQDY0101); xsl:copy of another node delivers the node, which the receiver copies.

Content LETs (glossary , sxml_ir_let.is_content, printed (let $n content ...)): a LET whose variable only the result of its block reads, first and in order; in a delivering task its bound expression delivers too. Lowering marks them with sxml_xpath_lowerer_mark_content_let (the block's open LET made for the item, else marking stops unless the item is ()). The machine also evaluates let $v := E return $v as E in place.

Lowerings: an XSLT literal result element, xsl:element, xsl:document and a temporary tree (9.4) compute their content in a block inside the constructor; a sequence constructor marks its children's LETs when it is a body or content (not with xsl:on-empty or xsl:on-non-empty, which read the atoms). XQuery computed element and document constructors do the same; a direct element constructor too, literal text as text constructors, unless two enclosed expressions are adjacent (<c>{1}{2}</c> stays a enclosed list). Other temporary trees (with-param, message bodies) still take their content as a value.
Arena nodes: content and in-scope namespaces share a union (a node has one or the other by kind), 72 to 56 bytes.

XSLT driver: result documents are collected only for assert-result-document (else the null handler, which still checks them); the evaluation step budget is 4 x the QT4 driver's (), as json-to-xml-013 takes about 190 million steps.

Measured (release, whole suites, before at 53bd400): json-to-xml-013 peaks at about 410 MB (2.1 GB before) and passes; XT40 in scope 7,986 to 7,987 of 8,728 (91.5 %), errors 1 to 0, no test set lost a case; XP40 30,647 and XQ40 40,034 passed, 0 errors; slices 198 and 147. The driver change was committed with 457f530 (packet ), which took the working tree's file.

Not done: XTDE3052 when an abstract variable is read (accept-042, -043a): v1-proxy is a global that reads the abstract v1, and globals are computed before the evaluation (XQuery's too, : only unreferenced ones are skipped), so a lazy error needs globals computed on first read, which a step function's synchronous atom reads cannot do today (Proposed). A RAISE read in place of the abstract variable alone was tried and dropped: v1-proxy still raises when it is computed.
